Shai Hope did not take the field on Day 2 and is still not with the team. Hope wasn't feeling well and did not travel with the side at the start of the day.
... SECOND INNINGS ...

The West Indies' bowling effort struggled with inconsistency throughout the innings, characterized by a lack of sustained pressure despite every bowler eventually managing to claim wickets. This lack of rhythm was exacerbated by a streak of poor fortune and a critical blow to their pace attack when Kemar Roach suffered a hamstring injury during the final moments of the opening day. His subsequent absence from the field on the second day left the attack depleted and unable to contain the New Zealand surge. To reclaim control of the match and secure a series victory, the West Indies must now focus on building a massive second-innings total that eclipses the visitors' lead, aiming to bat long enough to potentially avoid another outing with the and force a result in their favor.

Latham was eventually dismissed for a well-compiled 137 late on the first day, but Conway continued his brilliant form into day two, converting his century into a magnificent double-ton before his innings concluded at 227. The momentum continued with contributions from the entire batting order. Rachin Ravindra and Ajaz Patel remained unbeaten with scores of 72 and 29, respectively, when the declaration was made, ensuring a comprehensive team total of 575, which firmly places New Zealand in a commanding position.

In the pivotal third Test match, New Zealand asserted its dominance by posting a formidable total of 575 in the first innings on a challenging green pitch, setting a monumental asking track for the visiting team, hoping to level the series. The visitors, faced with this challenging total, saw their openers, Tom Latham and Devon Conway, start cautiously. However, once settled, their partnership blossomed into a historic 323-run stand for the first wicket, laying a rock-solid foundation for the rest of the batting lineup to build upon.

Commentary.Commentary: Despite losing Jacob Duffy and Kane Williamson, the hosts sit in a fairly comfortable position right now, thanks to a marathon innings from Devon Conway, who has already crossed his personal best and is now hungry for more. He too struggled initially but once the visitors started to bowl their second spells, Devon Conway pounced on the looseners quite effictively and if the tiredness pops up again in the second session, Devon Conway won't shy from taking them on yet again. West Indies have to grind hard for the wickets. Stay tuned for the second session.

Session Summary - 90 runs in 27 overs, losing 2 wickets. New Zealand have added 90 runs to the overnight total and continues to dominate this Test match but credit to West Indies for bowling with much more discipline today than they did yesterday. Despite bowling a bowler short, in the absence of Kemar Roach, Jayden Seales, Anderson Phillip and Justin Greaves grinded hard to keep things tight and beat the edge of Devon Conway and Kane Williamson numerous times. The opening pair of Devon Conway and Tom Latham didn't just put the Black Caps in a winning position, they completely rewrote the record books at Bay Oval. Latham and Conway set a new world record for the highest opening partnership in WTC history. They officially recorded the highest opening partnership ever on New Zealand soil.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the third and final Test between New Zealand and the West Indies at the picturesque Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui. Following a historic opening day, the Black Caps find themselves in a position of absolute command at 334/1.

And that’s a wrap on Day 1. The Kiwis are smiling and they have every reason for that. We’ll be firing back with action from Day 2 on December 19, 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, previous day). Tune in an hour early for the build-up. Cheers.

The skipper of New Zealand and one of the centurions, Tom Latham, is up for a chat. Tom Latham reflected on New Zealand's successful day with a mix of relief and pride, admitting to initial hesitation before the decision to bat first ultimately paid dividends. He credited the good day at the office to his partnership with Devon Conway, noting that Conway’s aggression acted as a vital counter-pressure valve against a West Indies attack that bowled with venom. While acknowledging the Windies' persistent hunt and late-day intensity, Latham remained delighted by his team's spark and the position they are in.

Inconsistent bowling by the West Indian bowling attack let the Kiwis pile glory unhindered. Kemar Roach and Jayden Seales flashed promise, but Anderson Phillip blinked crucially. Justin Greaves and Roston Chase troubled the batters but without any success, as Latham and Conway’s rock-solid defense was too good for the Windies' bowling attack. The first day of the 3rd Test has been owned by the home side, and the visitors must conjure a miracle with the ball first and then with the bat to salvage this battle.

The openers were a treat to watch for the fans of the game, riding the storm, capitalizing on the weak balls, and bowing respectfully to those landing just right. Until that tantalizing false stroke, swatted brilliantly by Roston Chase, ended the marathon opening stand of 323 for the Kiwis. Tom Latham departed after scoring 137, but Devon Conway still stands tall, unbeaten on 178. Jacob Duffy slipped in as a vigilant nightwatchman, ticking off 9 from 16, unbeaten and shielding his partner perfectly towards the end.

New Zealand blazed in, their openers fired on all cylinders, piling runs with swagger while the West Indies clawed at thin air. Conway and Latham walled in elegance, devoured the morning session, and paraded off as triumphant titans. The Windies, meanwhile, aimed wild, missing their bite, and handing the Kiwis a platter by going wicketless after the first session.

PITCH REPORT - Frances Mackay is thrilled to inspect the Bay Oval pitch. A fresh canvas ignites her passion. The strip wears a deceptive green cloak, 13mm of grass hints at aggression, but beneath lies a dry core. She forecasts an opening spell favoring pace and bounce, then nods to spin’s lurking charm as the game wears on. A golden toss win for New Zealand.

The skipper of the West Indies, Roston Chase, indicated that he felt good and would have elected to bowl first if he had won the toss, believing the team had a chance to win this Test match after showing fight in the first game but underperforming in the second. He announced one forced change to the side due to an injury to Ojay Shields, bringing Alick Athanaze into the team. Chase concluded that the West Indies still intended to utilize the grassy and green pitch conditions.

Tom Latham, the New Zealand captain, announced the team's decision to bat first based on past observations that spin becomes a factor later in the game. He acknowledged the challenge of the initial hours of a Test match but expressed hope that the team could successfully negotiate the first session. Latham stressed the team's desire to win while recognizing the hard work required and the need to adapt to the specific Mount Maunganui surface. He also confirmed one change to the playing eleven, with Ajaz Patel replacing Blair Tickner.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham (C), Devon Conway, Kane Williamson, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Glenn Phillips, Zakary Foulkes, Ajaz Patel, Jacob Duffy, Michael Rae.
West Indies (Playing XI) - John Campbell, Brandon King, Kavem Hodge, Shai Hope, Alick Athanaze, Roston Chase (C), Justin Greaves, Tevin Imlach (WK), Kemar Roach, Anderson Phillip, Jayden Seales.
TOSS - New Zealand have the coin flip and they will be batting first.

The West Indies arrive for this pivotal showdown having faced their share of adversity, with a necessary squad reshuffle driven by injuries. New Zealand, currently holding a precarious 1-0 series lead, enters the decider with its own adjustments, notably minus its half-century maker from the previous game, Mitchell Hay, who has been released from the squad with the inclusion of Tom Blundell. The Black Caps showcased their mettle in the last encounter, and now their bowlers are ready to unleash a vengeful intent once again. The West Indies batters must be wary and find a way to blunt the threat of Jacob Duffy, who led the charge with a devastating five-wicket haul in the previous match. The hosts are eager to harness their brawn and seal the deal on their home turf, but they know the tourists are capable of swooping in for a historic victory.
